# Empirical Evaluation and Clinical Validation

## Study Design, Biomedical Cohorts, and Synthetic Ground-Truth Regimes

We evaluate the nine architectures defined in Chapter 2 across twelve multi-view benchmarks: six real biomedical and clinical cohorts (`ADNI-MCI`, `MultiOmics` [TCGA-BRCA], `TCGA-KIRC`, `Heart`, `Diabetes`, and `mfeat`) and six synthetic generative regimes with known ground-truth latent coordinates $\mathbf{U}^*$ and feature supports $\mathbf{V}_m^*$ (@tbl-benchmark-cohorts). Every model is evaluated across three independent 70/30 stratified or random train/test splits (seeds $42, 43, 44$) across three `nsa_flow` quantile sparsity levels ($q \in \{\text{None}, 0.5, 0.8\}$, totaling $1,215$ cross-validation fits), supplemented by a $1,214$-configuration hyperparameter sweep on `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$). To prevent data leakage, all feature standardization (`StandardScaler`), column completeness filtering ($\ge 98\%$), and demographic covariate adjustments (Frisch–Waugh–Lovell residualization [@frisch1933partial; @lovell1963seasonal] of age, biological sex, and education inside `ADNI-MCI`) are fitted strictly within each training split and applied out-of-sample to the held-out test split.

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| label: tbl-benchmark-cohorts
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of the twelve multi-view benchmark cohorts (six clinical/biomedical datasets and six synthetic ground-truth generative regimes). Best out-of-sample scores across seeds 42–44 are computed directly from `deep_ranking_benchmark.csv`."
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import os
import pandas as pd
from tabulate import tabulate

csv_path = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_path):
    csv_path = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)
df["Model"] = df["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

cohort_meta = [
    ("ADNI-MCI", "Clinical MRI + Cog", 1084, "4 [160, 160, 62, 11]", "CogPC1 R2 (MRI Only)"),
    ("MultiOmics (BRCA)", "Oncology (mRNA/CNV/RPPA)", 822, "3 [200, 150, 150]", "ER Status Accuracy"),
    ("TCGA-KIRC", "Oncology (mRNA/CNV/RPPA)", 467, "3 [200, 150, 150]", "Pathologic Stage Acc"),
    ("Diabetes", "Clinical Chemistries", 442, "2 [5, 5]", "1-Yr Progression R2"),
    ("Heart", "Cardiology Vitals + ECG", 297, "2 [7, 6]", "Coronary Disease Acc"),
    ("mfeat", "Multi-Descriptor Digits", 2000, "4 [76, 64, 6, 47]", "10-Class Accuracy"),
    ("Linear", "Synthetic (50% Sparse ±)", 1000, "3 [100, 80, 60]", "Latent R2 & Support F1"),
    ("Polynomial", "Synthetic (Deg-3 Warped)", 1000, "3 [120, 80, 50]", "Latent R2 & CMC"),
    ("Sine", "Synthetic (Harmonic Warp)", 1000, "3 [120, 80, 50]", "Latent R2 & CMC"),
    ("Shared+Private", "Synthetic (80% Sparse ±)", 1000, "3 [160, 60, 30]", "Latent R2 & Support F1"),
    ("NonnegParts", "Synthetic (66.7% Non-Neg)", 400, "3 [120, 45, 30]", "Dominant Factor R2 & F1"),
    ("NonnegWeak", "Synthetic (80% Non-Neg)", 400, "3 [120, 45, 30]", "Weak Factor u3 R2 & F1"),
]

rows = []
for ds_label, domain, n_subj, views_str, task_str in cohort_meta:
    if "MultiOmics" in ds_label:
        ds_key = "MultiOmics"
    elif ds_label == "NonnegWeak":
        ds_key = "NonnegPartsWeak"
    else:
        ds_key = ds_label
    sub = df[df["Dataset"] == ds_key]
    agg_xv = sub.groupby("Model")["Strictly_Linear_Metric"].mean()
    pca_v = agg_xv["PCA"]
    best_m = agg_xv.idxmax()
    best_v = agg_xv.max()
    rows.append([
        ds_label,
        domain,
        f"{n_subj:,}",
        views_str,
        task_str,
        f"{best_m} ({best_v:.3f} vs PCA {pca_v:.3f})"
    ])

headers = ["Cohort", "Domain / Modality Structure", "N", "Views [p_m]", "Clinical / Task Target", "Best Linear XV vs PCA"]
print(tabulate(rows, headers=headers, tablefmt="pipe"))
```

In `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$) [@mueller2005; @jack2008alzheimer; @ADNI], Views 0–2 capture $382$ regional structural MRI features derived via the ANTs longitudinal and cross-sectional cortical thickness and Desikan–Killiany–Tourville (DKT) parcellation pipelines [@avants2008symmetric; @avants2011reproducible; @tustison2014large; @desikan2006automated; @klein2012mindboggle; @stone2020longitudinal; @stone2024blast; @Marek2011; @smith2013functional], while View 3 comprises eleven neuropsychological scales (`ADAS11`, `ADAS13`, `ADASQ4` [@rosen1984new], `MMSE` [@folstein1975mini], `CDRSB` [@morris1993clinical], `TRABSCOR` [@reitan1958validity], `FAQ` [@pfeffer1982measurement], and four Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test sub-scores `RAVLT_immediate`, `RAVLT_learning`, `RAVLT_forgetting`, `RAVLT_perc_forgetting` [@rey1964examen]). Following `Protocol B`, the three MRI views align with the cognitive battery during training, but test-set predictions are generated exclusively from structural MRI. In `MultiOmics` (`TCGA-BRCA`, $N = 822$) [@tcga2012breast] and `TCGA-KIRC` ($N = 467$) [@tcga2013kirc], mRNA expression ($p_1 = 200$), somatic copy-number variation ($p_2 = 150$), and RPPA proteomics ($p_3 = 150$) predict clinical Estrogen Receptor status and pathologic tumor stage, respectively.

## Global 12-Dataset Benchmark: Subspace Capacity vs. Single-Axis Interpretability

Across the $B = 12$ dataset blocks and nine architectures, block-averaged non-parametric Friedman [@friedman1937use] and Iman–Davenport [@Iman1980] omnibus tests confirm statistically significant differentiation on both the linear subspace probe ($\chi_F^2 = 31.49, p = 1.15 \times 10^{-4}$; $F_F = 5.37, p = 1.98 \times 10^{-5}$) and the multi-modal consensus probe ($\chi_F^2 = 20.87, p = 0.0075$; $F_F = 3.06, p = 0.0044$, Nemenyi Critical Difference $CD = 3.468$ at $\alpha = 0.05$ [@Demsar2006; @Nemenyi1963; @benavoli2016should]). @tbl-global-leaderboard summarizes the global metrics across all nine models, accompanied by the Demšar Critical Difference diagram (@fig-cd-diagram), the multi-objective speed–accuracy and support–consensus Pareto frontiers (@fig-pareto-frontier), and the three-probe performance profile (@fig-three-probes).

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| label: tbl-global-leaderboard
#| tbl-cap: "Global 12-dataset benchmark leaderboard across all nine architectures (mean across 12 cohorts and 3 random seeds at the canonical discovery operating point $q = 0.5$, paired with synthetic ground-truth recovery metrics). Directional arrows indicate optimization direction (↑ higher is better, ↓ lower is better)."
#| echo: false

import os
import sys
import pandas as pd
from tabulate import tabulate

csv_main = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_main):
    csv_main = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

csv_op = "results_cache/operating_points_05_08_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_op):
    csv_op = "paper/results_cache/operating_points_05_08_benchmark.csv"

df_main = pd.read_csv(csv_main)
df_main["Model"] = df_main["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

df_op = pd.read_csv(csv_op)
df_op["Model"] = df_op["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})
sub05 = df_op[df_op["Sparseness_Target"] == 0.5]

repo_root = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "..")) if "paper" in os.getcwd() else os.getcwd()
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(repo_root, "src"))
from pysimlr.benchmarks.deep_ranking import build_ranking_blocks, friedman_test

piv_xv, _ = build_ranking_blocks(df_main, metric_col="Strictly_Linear_Metric", floor_threshold=None)
f_xv = friedman_test(piv_xv.values, higher_is_better=True)
ranks_xv = pd.Series(f_xv["mean_ranks"], index=piv_xv.columns)

syn_df = sub05[sub05["Case_Type"] == "synthetic"]
syn_f1 = syn_df.groupby("Model")["Support_Recovery_V"].mean()
syn_cmc = df_main[df_main["Case_Type"] == "synthetic"].groupby("Model")["CMC_Latent_U"].mean()

agg05 = sub05.groupby("Model").agg({
    "Strictly_Linear_Metric": "mean",
    "Axis_Sensitive_Metric": "mean",
    "Predictive_Metric": "mean",
    "Sparsity_Ratio": "mean",
    "Fit_Seconds": "mean"
})

order = ranks_xv.sort_values().index.tolist()
rows = []
for m in order:
    lin_v = agg05.loc[m, "Strictly_Linear_Metric"]
    rf_v = agg05.loc[m, "Axis_Sensitive_Metric"]
    u_v = agg05.loc[m, "Predictive_Metric"]
    drop_v = rf_v - lin_v
    rows.append([
        m,
        f"{ranks_xv[m]:.2f}",
        f"{lin_v:.3f}",
        f"{rf_v:.3f} ({drop_v:+.3f})",
        f"{u_v:.3f}",
        f"{syn_cmc[m]:.3f}",
        f"{syn_f1[m]:.3f}",
        f"{agg05.loc[m, 'Sparsity_Ratio']*100:.1f}%"
    ])

headers = [
    "Architecture", "Friedman Rank ↓", "Linear XV ↑", "RF Axis XV (Drop) ↑",
    "Consensus U ↑", "Latent CMC ↑", "Support F1 ↑", "Sparsity % ↑"
]
print(tabulate(rows, headers=headers, tablefmt="pipe"))
```

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| label: fig-cd-diagram
#| fig-cap: "Demšar (2006) Critical Difference diagram across the $B = 12$ benchmark dataset blocks ($N = 36$ dataset-seed evaluations) for the linear entrypoint probe ($\\mathbf{X}\\mathbf{V}$, Friedman $\\chi_F^2 = 31.49, p = 1.15 \\times 10^{-4}$; Iman–Davenport $F_F = 5.37, p = 1.98 \\times 10^{-5}$). Horizontal axis plots mean rank (lower is better, $1 =$ best). Bold horizontal bars connect cliques of architectures whose rank differences are smaller than the Nemenyi Critical Difference ($CD = 3.468$ at $\\alpha = 0.05$). Green stars (`*`) indicate models on the 5-objective non-dominated Pareto frontier."
#| out-width: 100%
#| echo: false
import os
import sys
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

csv_main = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_main):
    csv_main = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

df_main = pd.read_csv(csv_main)
df_main["Model"] = df_main["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

repo_root = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "..")) if "paper" in os.getcwd() else os.getcwd()
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(repo_root, "src"))
from pysimlr.benchmarks.deep_ranking import build_ranking_blocks, friedman_test, compute_nemenyi_cd, compute_pareto_frontier

piv_xv, _ = build_ranking_blocks(df_main, metric_col="Strictly_Linear_Metric", floor_threshold=None)
f_xv = friedman_test(piv_xv.values, higher_is_better=True)
ranks = pd.Series(f_xv["mean_ranks"], index=piv_xv.columns).sort_values()
cd = compute_nemenyi_cd(piv_xv.shape[1], piv_xv.shape[0])

agg_all = df_main.groupby("Model", as_index=False).agg({
    "Predictive_Metric": "mean",
    "Strictly_Linear_Metric": "mean",
    "CMC_Latent_U": "mean",
    "Support_Recovery_V": "mean",
    "Fit_Seconds": "mean"
})
pareto_df = compute_pareto_frontier(
    agg_all,
    objectives=["Predictive_Metric", "Strictly_Linear_Metric", "CMC_Latent_U", "Support_Recovery_V", "Fit_Seconds"],
    maximize=[True, True, True, True, False]
)
pareto_set = set(pareto_df[pareto_df["is_pareto_optimal"]]["Model"])

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.5, 3.6), dpi=300)
ax.set_xlim(0.3, 9.7)
ax.set_ylim(0.0, 1.25)
ax.axis("off")

# Number line 1..9
y_axis = 0.92
ax.plot([1, 9], [y_axis, y_axis], color="#0f172a", lw=1.8)
for r_tick in range(1, 10):
    ax.plot([r_tick, r_tick], [y_axis - 0.035, y_axis + 0.035], color="#0f172a", lw=1.4)
    ax.text(r_tick, y_axis + 0.06, str(r_tick), ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9.5, weight="bold", color="#0f172a")

# Nemenyi CD reference bar at top left
cd_x0 = 1.0
cd_y = 1.15
ax.plot([cd_x0, cd_x0 + cd], [cd_y, cd_y], color="#dc2626", lw=2.4)
ax.plot([cd_x0, cd_x0], [cd_y - 0.03, cd_y + 0.03], color="#dc2626", lw=1.8)
ax.plot([cd_x0 + cd, cd_x0 + cd], [cd_y - 0.03, cd_y + 0.03], color="#dc2626", lw=1.8)
ax.text(cd_x0 + cd / 2, cd_y + 0.035, f"Nemenyi CD = {cd:.2f} (α = 0.05)", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9.0, weight="bold", color="#dc2626")

# Split models into left (top 5) and right (bottom 4)
n_left = 5
left_models = list(ranks.index[:n_left])
right_models = list(ranks.index[n_left:])

y_positions_left = np.linspace(0.62, 0.10, len(left_models))
for idx_m, m in enumerate(left_models):
    r_val = ranks[m]
    y_m = y_positions_left[idx_m]
    is_p = m in pareto_set
    col_m = "#059669" if is_p else "#0f172a"
    star = " *" if is_p else ""
    ax.plot([r_val, r_val], [y_axis, y_m], color="#475569", lw=1.1, linestyle="-")
    ax.plot([r_val, 0.85], [y_m, y_m], color="#475569", lw=1.1, linestyle="-")
    ax.plot(r_val, y_axis, "o", color=col_m, markersize=6.5)
    ax.text(0.80, y_m, f"{m}{star} ({r_val:.2f})", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=9.0, weight="bold", color=col_m)

y_positions_right = np.linspace(0.62, 0.16, len(right_models))
for idx_m, m in enumerate(right_models):
    r_val = ranks[m]
    y_m = y_positions_right[idx_m]
    is_p = m in pareto_set
    col_m = "#059669" if is_p else "#0f172a"
    star = " *" if is_p else ""
    ax.plot([r_val, r_val], [y_axis, y_m], color="#475569", lw=1.1, linestyle="-")
    ax.plot([r_val, 9.15], [y_m, y_m], color="#475569", lw=1.1, linestyle="-")
    ax.plot(r_val, y_axis, "o", color=col_m, markersize=6.5)
    ax.text(9.20, y_m, f"({r_val:.2f}) {m}{star}", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=9.0, weight="bold", color=col_m)

# Clique bars
r_vals = ranks.values
cliques = []
for i in range(len(r_vals)):
    j = i
    while j + 1 < len(r_vals) and (r_vals[j + 1] - r_vals[i]) <= cd:
        j += 1
    if j > i:
        is_sub = any(c_i <= i and j <= c_j for c_i, c_j in cliques)
        if not is_sub:
            cliques.append((i, j))

clique_y_base = 0.81
for c_idx, (i, j) in enumerate(cliques):
    cy = clique_y_base - c_idx * 0.065
    ax.plot([r_vals[i], r_vals[j]], [cy, cy], color="#1e293b", lw=4.0, solid_capstyle="round")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

(A) Out-of-sample multi-modal consensus performance ($\\mathbf{U}$) versus wall-clock execution time (`Fit_Seconds`, log scale), highlighting the 2D speed–accuracy Pareto frontier (green dashed envelope connecting `PCA`, `NSAFlow-PCA`, `SiMLR-LBFGS`, and `LEND`). #| out-width: 100%
#| echo: false
import os
import sys
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

csv_main = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_main):
    csv_main = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

df_main = pd.read_csv(csv_main)
df_main["Model"] = df_main["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

repo_root = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "..")) if "paper" in os.getcwd() else os.getcwd()
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(repo_root, "src"))
from pysimlr.benchmarks.deep_ranking import compute_pareto_frontier

agg_all = df_main.groupby("Model", as_index=False).agg({
    "Predictive_Metric": "mean",
    "Strictly_Linear_Metric": "mean",
    "CMC_Latent_U": "mean",
    "Support_Recovery_V": "mean",
    "Fit_Seconds": "mean"
})
p_df = compute_pareto_frontier(
    agg_all,
    objectives=["Predictive_Metric", "Strictly_Linear_Metric", "CMC_Latent_U", "Support_Recovery_V", "Fit_Seconds"],
    maximize=[True, True, True, True, False]
).set_index("Model")
syn_sub = df_main[df_main["Case_Type"] == "synthetic"].groupby("Model")[["CMC_Latent_U", "Support_Recovery_V"]].mean()

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11.2, 4.3), dpi=300, constrained_layout=True)

# Panel A: Consensus U vs Fit_Seconds
for m, row in p_df.iterrows():
    is_p = bool(row["is_pareto_optimal"])
    marker = "*" if is_p else "o"
    sz = 150 if is_p else 75
    col = "#059669" if is_p else "#475569"
    ax1.scatter(row["Fit_Seconds"], row["Predictive_Metric"], marker=marker, s=sz, color=col, edgecolor="#0f172a", lw=0.8, zorder=4)

offsets_a = {
    "PCA": (-28, -3),
    "NSAFlow-PCA": (8, 3),
    "SiMLR": (7, -4),
    "SiMLR-LBFGS": (8, 6),
    "SiMLR-LBFGSB": (8, -10),
    "LEND": (-14, 9),
    "NED": (-12, -14),
    "NEDPP": (8, -4),
    "Flow-SiMR-V": (-32, -14),
}
for m, row in p_df.iterrows():
    dx, dy = offsets_a.get(m, (6, 4))
    col_t = "#065f46" if row["is_pareto_optimal"] else "#1e293b"
    ax1.annotate(m, (row["Fit_Seconds"], row["Predictive_Metric"]), xytext=(dx, dy), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=8.2, weight="bold", color=col_t)

front_a = p_df.loc[["PCA", "NSAFlow-PCA", "SiMLR-LBFGS", "LEND"]]
ax1.plot(front_a["Fit_Seconds"], front_a["Predictive_Metric"], "--", color="#059669", lw=1.6, alpha=0.8, label="2D Speed–Accuracy Envelope")

ax1.set_xscale("log")
ax1.set_xlim(0.0005, 9.5)
ax1.set_ylim(0.60, 0.725)
ax1.set_xlabel("Mean Fit Time in Seconds (Log Scale, ↓ Faster)", fontsize=9.5, weight="bold")
ax1.set_ylabel("Out-of-Sample Consensus Score (U ↑)", fontsize=9.5, weight="bold")
ax1.set_title("A. Consensus Accuracy vs. Fit Time", fontsize=10.2, weight="bold")
ax1.grid(True, linestyle="--", alpha=0.35)
ax1.legend(loc="lower right", fontsize=8.2, frameon=True)

# Panel B: Support F1 vs CMC on Synthetic Regimes
for m in syn_sub.index:
    is_p = bool(p_df.loc[m, "is_pareto_optimal"])
    marker = "*" if is_p else "o"
    sz = 150 if is_p else 75
    col = "#059669" if is_p else "#475569"
    ax2.scatter(syn_sub.loc[m, "CMC_Latent_U"], syn_sub.loc[m, "Support_Recovery_V"], marker=marker, s=sz, color=col, edgecolor="#0f172a", lw=0.8, zorder=4)

offsets_b = {
    "SiMLR": (-36, -4),
    "SiMLR-LBFGSB": (-74, 5),
    "SiMLR-LBFGS": (-70, -10),
    "NSAFlow-PCA": (8, -5),
    "LEND": (5, 7),
    "NED": (7, 4),
    "NEDPP": (-42, -4),
    "Flow-SiMR-V": (8, -2),
    "PCA": (8, 4),
}
for m in syn_sub.index:
    dx, dy = offsets_b.get(m, (6, 4))
    col_t = "#065f46" if p_df.loc[m, "is_pareto_optimal"] else "#1e293b"
    ax2.annotate(m, (syn_sub.loc[m, "CMC_Latent_U"], syn_sub.loc[m, "Support_Recovery_V"]), xytext=(dx, dy), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=8.2, weight="bold", color=col_t)

ax2.set_xlim(0.32, 0.95)
ax2.set_ylim(-0.04, 0.74)
ax2.set_xlabel("Latent Manifold Recovery on U (CMC ↑)", fontsize=9.5, weight="bold")
ax2.set_ylabel("Pathway Support Recovery on V (Jaccard F1 ↑)", fontsize=9.5, weight="bold")
ax2.set_title("B. Sparse Support Recovery vs. Latent Manifold CMC", fontsize=10.2, weight="bold")
ax2.grid(True, linestyle="--", alpha=0.35)

plt.show()

Single-matrix `PCA` suffers double the axis-sensitive Random Forest degradation ($\\Delta = -0.044$) compared to coordinate-aligned SiMR models (`SiMLR-LBFGSB` $\\Delta = -0.022$, `Flow-SiMR-V` $\\Delta = -0.024$) because dense eigenvectors mix biological mechanisms across coordinates."
#| out-width: 100%

import os
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

csv_op = "results_cache/operating_points_05_08_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_op):
    csv_op = "paper/results_cache/operating_points_05_08_benchmark.csv"

df_op = pd.read_csv(csv_op)
df_op["Model"] = df_op["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

sub05 = df_op[df_op["Sparseness_Target"] == 0.5]
piv_probes = sub05.groupby("Model")[["Strictly_Linear_Metric", "Axis_Sensitive_Metric", "Predictive_Metric"]].mean()
model_order = ["LEND", "Flow-SiMR-V", "SiMLR-LBFGSB", "SiMLR-LBFGS", "SiMLR", "NEDPP", "NED", "NSAFlow-PCA", "PCA"]
piv_probes = piv_probes.reindex([m for m in model_order if m in piv_probes.index])

fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.8, 3.9), dpi=300)

x = np.arange(len(piv_probes))
width = 0.26
b1 = ax1.bar(x - width, piv_probes["Strictly_Linear_Metric"], width, label="1. Subspace Fidelity: Ridge(XV) ↑", color="#0284c7", edgecolor="#0f172a", lw=0.7)
b2 = ax1.bar(x, piv_probes["Axis_Sensitive_Metric"], width, label="2. Single-Axis Interpretability: RandomForest(XV) ↑", color="#0d9488", edgecolor="#0f172a", lw=0.7)
b3 = ax1.bar(x + width, piv_probes["Predictive_Metric"], width, label="3. Multi-Modal Consensus: Ridge(U) ↑", color="#d97706", edgecolor="#0f172a", lw=0.7)

for bars in (b1, b2, b3):

        ax1.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, h + 0.004, f"{h:.2f}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=7.2, weight="bold", color="#1e293b")

ax1.set_ylabel("Mean Out-of-Sample Score (↑)", fontsize=9.8, weight="bold")

pca_idx = list(piv_probes.index).index("PCA")
ax1.annotate("PCA Diagonal Axis Mixing Drop\n(RF Drop Δ = -0.0439 vs SiMLR -0.022)",
             xy=(pca_idx, piv_probes.loc["PCA", "Axis_Sensitive_Metric"]),

Three empirical principles emerge from @tbl-global-leaderboard and Figures [-@fig-cd-diagram]–[-@fig-three-probes]:

1. **Multi-View Alignment Outperforms Single-Matrix Factorization When Views Differ in Scale or Private Variance**: `LEND` (mean Friedman rank $3.79$), `NED` ($3.88$), `NEDPP` ($3.92$), and `Flow-SiMR-V` ($4.25$) lead the linear entrypoint ranking ahead of concatenated `PCA` ($7.75$) and `NSAFlow-PCA` ($7.67$). On heterogeneous cohorts such as `mfeat` ($p = [76, 64, 6, 47]$) and `Shared+Private` ($p = [160, 60, 30]$), concatenated `PCA` rotates toward the highest-dimensional view (`mfeat` linear accuracy $0.727$, `Shared+Private` $R^2 = 0.618$), whereas cross-view alignment equalizes view contributions (`mfeat` accuracy $0.964$ for `NEDPP` and $0.948$ for `SiMLR-LBFGSB`; `Shared+Private` $R^2 = 0.956$ for `LEND`).
2. **Coordinate-Aligned `nsa_flow` Projections Prevent the Random Forest Axis Drop**: As established in @eq-subspace-invariance, ridge regression on $\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ is insensitive to orthogonal or oblique column mixing $\mathbf{V}_m \mathbf{M}$, hiding the fact that dense `PCA` mixes distinct biological mechanisms across columns. When evaluated with coordinate-splitting decision trees (`RandomForest`), `PCA` suffers an average score drop of $\Delta = -0.044$ across the 12 cohorts—collapsing completely on weak sparse factors (`NonnegPartsWeak` linear $R^2 = 0.125 \to$ Random Forest $R^2 = 0.000$) and dropping by $71\%$ on `ADNI-MCI` ($0.152 \to 0.044$). In contrast, `Flow-SiMR-V` ($\Delta = -0.022$) and `LEND` ($\Delta = -0.023$) cut the axis-mixing penalty in half.
3. **Operating Points Match Intrinsic Biological Density ($q = 0.5$ vs. $q = 0.8$)**: @fig-operating-point-and-support demonstrates how the quantile threshold $q$ acts as a tunable lens on feature support recovery. Across the $1,215$-fit operating-point evaluation, moderate sparsity ($q = 0.5$) achieves the highest overall linear predictive score ($0.680$) and highest Random Forest axis score ($0.651$) while recovering $F_1 = 0.989$ (`SiMLR-LBFGSB` on `NonnegParts`) and $F_1 = 0.709$–$1.000$ on $50\%$-sparse ground-truth pathways (`Linear`). When the underlying biology is concentrated in focal $20\%$-active modules (`NonnegPartsWeak` and `Shared+Private`), increasing the quantile threshold to $q = 0.8$ raises support recovery to $F_1 = 0.797$ while preserving $99.1\%$ of peak subspace accuracy ($0.674$ vs. $0.680$).

## Clinical Neuroimaging in `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$): Predicting Cognitive Decline and Mapping Braak Staging from MRI Alone

A primary clinical test of multi-modal representation learning is whether aligning structural neuroimaging with multi-domain cognitive batteries during training yields an anatomical basis that better predicts cognitive severity in new patients who have only undergone an MRI scan (`Protocol B`). Across $N = 1,084$ participants with Mild Cognitive Impairment, @tbl-adni-mci-summary compares all nine benchmark models on held-out MRI-only prediction of composite cognitive impairment (`CogPC1` $R^2$, after in-fold adjustment for age, sex, and education), single-axis Random Forest prediction, and mean ridge regression $R^2$ across all eleven individual neuropsychological scales (`ADAS11`, `ADAS13`, `ADASQ4`, `MMSE`, `CDRSB`, `TRABSCOR`, `FAQ`, and four `RAVLT` memory scales).

Comparing the unsupervised anatomical baselines against cognitive-aligned SiMR models in @tbl-adni-mci-summary and @fig-adni-neuroanatomy-flagship yields three core clinical and neurobiological insights:

1. **Supervising MRI Factor Discovery with Cognitive Batteries Improves Out-of-Sample MRI Prediction by $+65.8\%$**: Unsupervised `PCA` on the $382$ structural MRI features explains $R^2 = 0.152 \pm 0.004$ of out-of-sample cognitive variance on the linear probe and collapses to $R^2 = 0.044$ on the single-axis Random Forest probe because its leading component reflects global head and brain size rather than focal neurodegeneration. Aligning the MRI projections against the 11-scale cognitive battery during training raises out-of-sample MRI-only `CogPC1` prediction to $R^2 = 0.252 \pm 0.008$ (`LEND`), $0.231 \pm 0.015$ (`Flow-SiMR-V`, with Random Forest axis $R^2 = 0.197$, a $4.5\times$ improvement over `PCA`), and $0.241$ for linear `SiMLR` solvers in the $1,214$-configuration sweep, while raising mean prediction across all eleven individual cognitive scales by $+32.1\%$ ($R^2 = 0.107$ vs. $0.081$ for `PCA`; peaking on `ADAS13` $R^2 = 0.195$, `ADAS11` $0.165$, and `MMSE` $0.141$).
2. **Orthogonal Varimax Subspace Rotation and Quantile-Sparsified Non-Negative SiMR ($q = 0.85$) Isolate Three Classical Braak Neurofibrillary Networks**: As shown in @fig-adni-neuroanatomy-flagship, dense `PCA` (Panel A1) assigns nearly uniform negative weights ($\approx -0.15$) across all $62$ DKT cortical thickness parcels on Component 1 ($0\%$ sparsity), mixing temporoparietal association areas with primary motor and visual cortices. Under unrotated PCA initialization without quantile thresholding (Panel A2, `varimax = False, q = None`), Component 1 absorbs this positive global correlation floor across $53/62$ regions ($15\%$ overall sparsity). Enabling default orthogonal Varimax subspace rotation (`varimax = True` in `pysimlr v0.2.17`, Panel A3) rotates the $3$-dimensional subspace before non-negative `nsa_flow` retraction, immediately raising unthresholded sparsity from $15\%$ to $66\%$ with balanced active supports ($[24, 12, 26]$ DKT parcels across $\mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_2, \mathbf{v}_3$) without requiring manual subject row-mean centering. Combining non-negative `nsa_flow` ($w = 0.50$) with `sparseness = 0.85` (Panels A4 and B) further restricts each latent axis to $9/62$ active DKT regions ($88\%$ overall sparsity, Gram defect $D = 8.2 \times 10^{-5}$) while achieving higher out-of-sample cognitive accuracy ($R^2 = 0.192$) than dense `PCA` ($0.190$):
   * **Component 1 ($\mathbf{v}_1$, Temporoparietal Association Network — Braak Stages IV–V)**: Concentrates weight in `left_middle_temporal` ($+0.670$), `left_supramarginal` ($+0.454$), `right_middle_temporal` ($+0.341$), `right_pars_opercularis` ($+0.319$), and `left_superior_frontal` ($+0.209$). Thinning across these heteromodal temporoparietal and inferior frontal hubs marks the clinical transition from isolated amnestic impairment to language, semantic, and praxis decline [@braak1991neuropathological; @dickerson2009cortical; @buckner2005].
   * **Component 2 ($\mathbf{v}_2$, Medial Temporal Amnestic Core — Braak Stages I–III)**: Isolates bilateral entorhinal cortex (`left_entorhinal` $+0.680$, `right_entorhinal` $+0.226$) and precuneal/cuneal posterior hubs (`right_cuneus` $+0.698$), coupled with subcortical hippocampal volume loss in View 0 (`right_hippocampus` $+0.369$). This circuit directly reflects early transentorhinal tau neurofibrillary pathology responsible for episodic memory encoding failure on `RAVLT` and `ADASQ4` [@braak1991neuropathological; @jack2018nia; @rey1964examen].
   * **Component 3 ($\mathbf{v}_3$, Frontocingulate Salience Network)**: Targets `left_rostral_middle_frontal` ($+0.631$), `right_caudal_anterior_cingulate` ($+0.478$), and bilateral insular cortex (`left_insula` $+0.434$, `right_insula` $+0.429$). Atrophy in this anterior cingulate–insular salience network [@seeley2009neurodegenerative; @menon2010saliency] governs executive set-shifting deficits (`TRABSCOR` [@reitan1958validity]) and everyday functional decline (`FAQ` [@pfeffer1982measurement]).
3. **Spared Primary Sensorimotor Cortex and Support-Shuffled / PCA-Rotated Score Controls Confirm True Anatomical Localization**: Across all three components, primary motor cortex (`right_precentral` $+0.0016$, `left_precentral` $\le 10^{-5}$) and primary somatosensory cortex (`left_postcentral` $\le 10^{-5}$, `right_postcentral` $\le 10^{-5}$) receive effectively zero weight (@fig-adni-neuroanatomy-flagship B). Because primary sensorimotor neocortex is pathologically spared until end-stage Alzheimer's disease [@braak1991neuropathological; @dickerson2009cortical], its automatic exclusion provides an internal neurobiological control. To further separate coordinate-level axis alignment and anatomical support localization from pure subspace capacity, we evaluate two algorithmic negative controls across all 3 seeds on `ADNI-MCI` (`adni_mci_axis_alignment_controls.csv` via `axis_alignment_control_metrics`): (i) a **PCA-Rotated Score Control** that rotates the learned scores $\mathbf{Z} = [\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m]$ by their in-fold principal-component eigenvectors $\mathbf{Q} \in \mathrm{O}(Mk)$ ($\operatorname{span}(\mathbf{Z}\mathbf{Q}) = \operatorname{span}(\mathbf{Z})$), which leaves the linear probe identically unchanged to machine precision (`Flow-SiMR-V` $0.2403 \to 0.2403$; `LEND` $0.2418 \to 0.2418$; `SiMLR-LBFGSB` $0.1650 \to 0.1650$) while reducing single-axis Random Forest accuracy when localized axes are mixed (`SiMLR-LBFGSB` $0.1123 \to 0.0879$, `LEND` non-negative $0.1617 \to 0.1416$); and (ii) a **Support-Shuffled Basis Control** that permutes the row indices of each $\mathbf{V}_m$ within view $m$ ($\mathbf{V}_m[\pi_m, :]$, preserving exact sparsity, weight magnitudes, and Stiefel orthogonality $\mathbf{V}_m^\top \mathbf{V}_m$), which collapses the Random Forest `CogPC1` $R^2$ by $60\%$–$65\%$ (`Flow-SiMR-V` $0.1798 \to 0.0627$, $\Delta = -0.1171$; `LEND` $0.1725 \to 0.0690$, $\Delta = -0.1035$; `NEDPP` $0.1563 \to 0.0668$, $\Delta = -0.0895$) and linear $R^2$ from $0.240$–$0.242$ to $0.151$–$0.157$ (the unstructured `PCA` baseline floor of $0.151$). This confirms that the $+3.8\times$ to $+4.5\times$ Random Forest advantage on `ADNI-MCI` arises directly from localizing true neuroanatomical circuits rather than generic sparsity or basis conditioning.

signature_regions = [
    ("L middle temporal", "left_middle_temporal", "Net 1: Temporoparietal (Braak IV-V)", "#0284c7"),
    ("L supramarginal", "left_supramarginal", "Net 1: Temporoparietal (Braak IV-V)", "#0284c7"),
    ("R middle temporal", "right_middle_temporal", "Net 1: Temporoparietal (Braak IV-V)", "#0284c7"),
    ("R pars opercularis", "right_pars_opercularis", "Net 1: Temporoparietal (Braak IV-V)", "#0284c7"),
    ("R cuneus", "right_cuneus", "Net 2: Medial Temporal (Braak I-III)", "#0d9488"),
    ("L entorhinal", "left_entorhinal", "Net 2: Medial Temporal (Braak I-III)", "#0d9488"),
    ("R entorhinal", "right_entorhinal", "Net 2: Medial Temporal (Braak I-III)", "#0d9488"),
    ("L rostral mid frontal", "left_rostral_middle_frontal", "Net 3: Frontocingulate Salience", "#7c3aed"),
    ("R caudal ant cingulate", "right_caudal_anterior_cingulate", "Net 3: Frontocingulate Salience", "#7c3aed"),
    ("L insula", "left_insula", "Net 3: Frontocingulate Salience", "#7c3aed"),
    ("R insula", "right_insula", "Net 3: Frontocingulate Salience", "#7c3aed"),
    ("R precentral (Motor)", "right_precentral", "Spared Primary Sensorimotor Control", "#94a3b8"),
    ("L precentral (Motor)", "left_precentral", "Spared Primary Sensorimotor Control", "#94a3b8"),
    ("L postcentral (Sensory)", "left_postcentral", "Spared Primary Sensorimotor Control", "#94a3b8"),
]

y_b = np.arange(len(signature_regions))
vals_b, cols_b, labels_b = [], [], []
for disp_nm, key_nm, grp_nm, col_hex in signature_regions:
    idx_r = raw_names.index(key_nm)
    if "Net 1" in grp_nm:
        v = mat_q85[idx_r, 0]
    elif "Net 2" in grp_nm:
        v = mat_q85[idx_r, 1]
    elif "Net 3" in grp_nm:
        v = mat_q85[idx_r, 2]
    else:
        v = np.max(mat_q85[idx_r, :])
    vals_b.append(v)
    cols_b.append(col_hex)
    labels_b.append(disp_nm)

ax_bars.barh(y_b, vals_b, color=cols_b, edgecolor="#0f172a", height=0.68, lw=0.7)
for idx_i, val_i in enumerate(vals_b):
    txt = f"{val_i:.3f}" if val_i > 0.005 else "0.000 (Spared Negative Control)"
    ax_bars.text(val_i + 0.012, idx_i, txt, va="center", fontsize=8.4, weight="bold", color="#0f172a")

ax_bars.invert_yaxis()
ax_bars.set_yticks(y_b)
ax_bars.set_yticklabels(labels_b, fontsize=8.5, weight="bold")
ax_bars.set_xlim(0, 0.86)
ax_bars.set_xlabel("Normalized Non-Negative Basis Loading (V₂)", fontsize=9.5, weight="bold")
ax_bars.set_title("B. Isolated Braak Neurofibrillary Circuits & Spared Primary Sensorimotor Cortex (Focal SiMR q = 0.85)", fontsize=10.0, weight="bold")
ax_bars.grid(True, axis="x", linestyle="--", alpha=0.35)

legend_patches = [
    Patch(facecolor="#0284c7", edgecolor="#0f172a", label="Net 1: Temporoparietal Association (Braak IV-V)"),
    Patch(facecolor="#0d9488", edgecolor="#0f172a", label="Net 2: Medial Temporal Amnestic Core (Braak I-III)"),
    Patch(facecolor="#7c3aed", edgecolor="#0f172a", label="Net 3: Frontocingulate Salience Network"),
    Patch(facecolor="#94a3b8", edgecolor="#0f172a", label="Spared Primary Sensorimotor Control (≈ 0)")
]
ax_bars.legend(handles=legend_patches, loc="lower right", fontsize=8.4, frameon=True)

plt.show()
```

## Multi-Omic Oncology (`TCGA-BRCA`, `TCGA-KIRC`) and Patient-Level Clinical Attribution

To verify that the same architectural principles generalize beyond neuroimaging to molecular oncology and clinical tabular medicine, @tbl-real-cohorts-summary compares all nine models across the six real cohorts, @fig-multiomics-and-patient-attribution illustrates cross-cohort performance alongside exact patient-level clinical risk decomposition (`Diabetes` Patient #1 and `Heart` Patient #122 in @fig-heart-audit), and @fig-nsa-v-interpretability demonstrates how `nsa_flow` preserves localized hierarchical basis weights across modalities.

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| label: tbl-real-cohorts-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Out-of-sample linear entrypoint performance (`XV`, top) and multi-modal consensus performance (`U`, bottom) across all six real biomedical cohorts (3-seed mean from `deep_ranking_benchmark.csv`, higher is better ↑)."
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import os
import pandas as pd
from tabulate import tabulate

csv_path = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_path):
    csv_path = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)
df["Model"] = df["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

models = ["LEND", "Flow-SiMR-V", "SiMLR-LBFGSB", "SiMLR-LBFGS", "SiMLR", "NEDPP", "NED", "NSAFlow-PCA", "PCA"]

rows = []

    row = [m]
    for ds in real_dsets:
        sub = df[(df["Dataset"] == ds) & (df["Model"] == m)]
        xv_m = sub["Strictly_Linear_Metric"].mean()

    rows.append(row)

headers = [
    "Architecture", "ADNI-MCI R2 ↑", "TCGA-BRCA Acc ↑", "TCGA-KIRC Acc ↑",
    "Diabetes R2 ↑", "Heart Acc ↑", "mfeat Acc ↑"
]
print(tabulate(rows, headers=headers, tablefmt="pipe"))

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| label: fig-multiomics-and-patient-attribution
#| fig-cap: "Multi-cohort biomedical performance and exact patient-level feature attribution. (A) Out-of-sample linear entrypoint scores across the six real cohorts comparing best SiMR architectures (`LEND`, `Flow-SiMR-V`, `SiMLR-LBFGSB`) against dense `PCA`. (B) Exact additive patient-level risk attribution ($c_{ij} = x_{ij} v_{jl}$) on the Diabetes cohort (Patient #1), decomposing the patient's progression score directly into standardized clinical vitals without post-hoc Monte Carlo perturbation."
#| out-width: 100%
#| echo: false
import os
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.datasets import load_diabetes
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from pysimlr import simlr

csv_path = "results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"
if not os.path.exists(csv_path):
    csv_path = "paper/results_cache/deep_ranking_benchmark.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)
df["Model"] = df["Model"].replace({"Flow-SiMLR-V": "Flow-SiMR-V", "Flow-SiMLR": "Flow-SiMR"})

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11.2, 4.1), dpi=300, gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1.3, 1.0]}, constrained_layout=True)

real_dsets = ["ADNI-MCI", "MultiOmics", "TCGA-KIRC", "Diabetes", "Heart", "mfeat"]
disp_names = ["ADNI-MCI\n(MRI→Cog)", "TCGA-BRCA\n(ER Acc)", "TCGA-KIRC\n(Stage Acc)", "Diabetes\n(Prog R²)", "Heart\n(CAD Acc)", "mfeat\n(Digit Acc)"]

piv_r = df[df["Dataset"].isin(real_dsets)].pivot_table(index="Dataset", columns="Model", values="Strictly_Linear_Metric", aggfunc="mean").reindex(real_dsets)

x = np.arange(len(real_dsets))
w = 0.20
ax1.bar(x - 1.5*w, piv_r["LEND"], w, label="LEND", color="#0284c7", edgecolor="#0f172a", lw=0.7)
ax1.bar(x - 0.5*w, piv_r["Flow-SiMR-V"], w, label="Flow-SiMR-V", color="#0d9488", edgecolor="#0f172a", lw=0.7)
ax1.bar(x + 0.5*w, piv_r["SiMLR-LBFGSB"], w, label="SiMLR-LBFGSB", color="#7c3aed", edgecolor="#0f172a", lw=0.7)
ax1.bar(x + 1.5*w, piv_r["PCA"], w, label="Dense PCA", color="#94a3b8", edgecolor="#0f172a", lw=0.7)

ax1.set_xticks(x)
ax1.set_xticklabels(disp_names, fontsize=8.2, weight="bold")
ax1.set_ylabel("Out-of-Sample Linear Probe Score (↑)", fontsize=9.5, weight="bold")
ax1.set_title("A. Multi-View SiMR vs. Dense PCA Across Real Cohorts", fontsize=10.0, weight="bold")
ax1.set_ylim(0.10, 1.05)
ax1.grid(True, axis="y", linestyle="--", alpha=0.35)
ax1.legend(loc="upper left", ncol=2, fontsize=8.0, frameon=True)

# Panel B: Exact Patient-Level Feature Attribution on Diabetes
np.random.seed(42)
data = load_diabetes()
X_scaled = StandardScaler().fit_transform(data.data)
res_db = simlr([X_scaled[:, :5], X_scaled[:, 5:]], k=2, optimizer="lbfgsb", positivity="positive", sparseness=0.5, random_state=42)
v_db = np.asarray(res_db["v"][0])
x_sample = X_scaled[0, :5]
impact = x_sample * v_db[:, 0]
feat_names = ["Age", "Sex", "Body Mass Index", "Mean Blood Pressure", "Total Cholesterol"]

idx = np.argsort(np.abs(impact))[::-1]
colors = ["#dc2626" if impact[i] >= 0 else "#0284c7" for i in idx]
y_pos = np.arange(len(idx))
ax2.barh(y_pos, impact[idx], color=colors, edgecolor="#0f172a", height=0.58, lw=0.7)

min_imp = float(np.min(impact))
max_imp = float(np.max(impact))
span = max(max_imp - min_imp, 0.5)
ax2.set_xlim(min_imp - 0.30 * span, max_imp + 0.30 * span)

for pos_i, orig_i in enumerate(idx):
    val_i = float(impact[orig_i])
    if val_i >= 0:
        ax2.text(val_i + 0.03 * span, pos_i, f"{val_i:+.2f}", va="center", ha="left", fontsize=8.4, weight="bold", color="#0f172a")
    else:
        ax2.text(val_i - 0.03 * span, pos_i, f"{val_i:+.2f}", va="center", ha="right", fontsize=8.4, weight="bold", color="#0f172a")

ax2.invert_yaxis()
ax2.set_yticks(y_pos)
ax2.set_yticklabels([feat_names[i] for i in idx], fontsize=8.5, weight="bold")
ax2.axvline(0, color="#0f172a", lw=0.9)
ax2.set_xlabel("Exact Additive Contribution (x_ij · v_jl)", fontsize=9.5, weight="bold")
ax2.set_title("B. Exact Patient-Level Risk Attribution (Patient #1)", fontsize=10.0, weight="bold")
ax2.grid(True, axis="x", linestyle="--", alpha=0.35)

plt.show()
```

::: {.column width="48%"}
![**Cardiology Patient-Level Risk Decomposition (`Heart` Cohort, Patient #122).** Exact additive feature contributions $c_{ij} = x_{ij} v_{jl}$ on the linear entrypoint decompose individual coronary artery disease risk directly into standardized clinical vitals and ECG indicators (`ca` fluoroscopy vessels, `thal` thallium defect, `oldpeak` ST depression, `exang` exercise angina).](figures/heart_waterfall.png){#fig-heart-audit width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="4%"}
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
![**Hierarchical Sparse Basis Localization (`varimax + nsa_flow`).** Orthogonal Varimax subspace rotation paired with Non-Negative Stiefel Approximating Flow ($q = 0.50$) partitions every clinical and biomarker view of `Heart` and `Diabetes` into balanced, non-overlapping physiological subnetworks (`L1` vs. `L2`, Gini $G \in [0.51, 0.77]$), eliminating the unrotated `"Component 1 = Mean"` imbalance.](figures/nsa_v_interpretability.png){#fig-nsa-v-interpretability width="100%"}
:::
::::

In `MultiOmics` (`TCGA-BRCA`, $N = 822$), `Flow-SiMR-V`, `LEND`, and `NEDPP` achieve $92.7\% \pm 0.7\%$ out-of-sample Estrogen Receptor classification accuracy (vs. $91.5\%$ for `PCA`), while the sparse non-negative dictionaries $\mathbf{V}_m$ isolate the canonical luminal breast cancer signaling cascade across all three molecular layers (detailed in Appendix A): estrogen receptor alpha (`ER-alpha`) and phosphorylated `ER-alpha_pS118` in RPPA proteomics, master luminal transcription factors `GATA3`, `PGR`, and `ESR1` in mRNA transcriptomics [@perou2000; @parker2009supervised], and focal chromosomal amplifications at `17q23` and `8p11-p12` in somatic copy-number variation [@tcga2012breast; @curtis2012]. In `TCGA-KIRC` ($N = 467$), adding non-linear decoding in `LEND` improves pathologic stage classification on the consensus embedding $\mathbf{U}$ to $71.4\% \pm 0.4\%$ (vs. $67.1\%$ for `PCA`), capturing non-linear metabolic and hypoxia-inducible interactions across transcriptomic and proteomic layers [@tcga2013kirc]. Finally, on compact clinical cohorts (`Diabetes` $R^2 = 0.396$ for `SiMLR-LBFGSB` vs. $0.351$ for `PCA`; `Heart` accuracy $0.848$ for `NSAFlow-PCA`), pairing orthogonal Varimax subspace rotation with `nsa_flow` ($q = 0.50$) cleanly separates each modality into balanced physiological subnetworks (@fig-nsa-v-interpretability)—isolating resting hemodynamics (`trestbps` $0.91$, `restecg` $0.42$) from chest-pain and demographic profile (`cp` $0.70$, `sex` $0.63$, `age` $0.32$) in `Heart` View 1, exercise ST/heart-rate response (`oldpeak` $0.73$, `thalach` $0.50$, `slope` $0.46$) from perfusion/vessel burden (`thal` $0.75$, `exang` $0.57$, `ca` $0.34$) in `Heart` View 2, adiposity/blood pressure (`bp` $0.73$, `bmi` $0.68$) from age/sex (`age` $0.78$, `sex` $0.62$) in `Diabetes` View 1, and the glycemic/triglyceride triad (`s5` $0.63$, `s6` $0.56$, `s4` $0.54$) from lipoprotein cholesterol (`s2` $0.71$, `s1` $0.70$) in `Diabetes` View 2—while the linear entrypoint $\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ decomposes any individual patient's risk score into exact feature-level clinical contributions $c_{m,i,j,l} = x_{m,i,j} v_{m,j,l}$ without post-hoc Monte Carlo approximations [@Wachter_2017; @karimi2021algorithmic; @pearl2009causality] (@fig-multiomics-and-patient-attribution B and @fig-heart-audit). Complete parameter sensitivity ablations—including the $w \in [0.01, 0.95]$ trade-off curve, row-mean/ICA preprocessing controls, latent rank $k \in \{2, 3, 5, 8\}$ scaling, and pairwise Wilcoxon rank-sum tests—are provided in Appendix B.
